comment:
The owner: "signage is unclear and I think the wall decor scheme doesn't fit too well."
1. Signage: each of the six wood merchants must say what it sells, clearly, from across the street. Today the names are small, low-contrast letters lost in the awnings. Give each shop a big, high-contrast name board on its fascia (banner or block letters, light on dark or dark on light, the full width of the shop: OAK, SPRUCE, BIRCH, JUNGLE, ACACIA, DARK OAK), and a hanging sign on a bracket with that wood's emblem at y 4 or higher. Keep the fascias over the socket fronts and out of the 2 cells in front of the counters (sockets.json; check with $MCD sockets check build.nbt).
2. Wall decor: the half-timbering reads as noise (the scattered calcite pattern on the gables especially) and doesn't fit a working timber warehouse. Make the frame scheme calm and regular: the same post spacing on every storey, posts lined up over the shop piers, straight rails at each floor, and a simple, repeated brace, so the gables and long sides read as one frame.
summary: Each shop now has a full-width name board with white banner letters on dark oak, plus a hanging blade sign showing its wood. The frame is regular: the same posts on both storeys and gables, one brace in every closed bay, and plain calcite between. `mcd sockets check` shows 12 sockets with 0 problems, all 14 rooms are still walkable, and `mcd check` reports no floating or unsupported blocks. The 22 orphans are existing counter slabs; I did not touch them.
applied: Name boards: I removed the sloping awnings that hid the names. Each fascia is now a dark oak board with a course of the shop's own planks and a lip of its own stairs along the top. The names stand on a plank ledge at z4 y9 (z33 on the south street), so they don't float.

Letters are white on dark, one per character, across the whole 7-wide frontage. OAK is spaced out as O A K to fill its board. Boards stay on z5/z32, y9..11, and nothing was added to the 2 cells in front of the counters.

Hanging signs: I replaced the blank edge-on blades with one blade per business on a fence arm at y11, hung at y9..10. Its street end shows the wood's log end over its leaves, and its sides show rings over leaves. They are placed off the letters.
Frame: posts are now x 2, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, 33, 37, 40 on both storeys and both streets. I dropped the odd extra door posts at x10 and x32, so every post sits over a pier or wall line.

Frame: closed bays all use the same brace, including the two end bays that used a different one. Door bays keep the loading doors at x11..12 and x30..31 with one calcite cell beside them. The head plates and cornice stay straight.

Gables: I replaced the scattered braces and king posts with a simple frame: the storey posts carried up to the rafters (x 5, 9, 13, 17 and 25, 29, 33, 37), one straight tie beam at y28, a single brace in each outer bay, and plain calcite. The gable door columns at x11..12 and x30..31 are now left open for the loading doors.
skipped: The fascia on the south street's dark oak shop still reads DK OAK, not DARK OAK. Eight characters don't fit on a 7-cell banner board, and widening it would take the pier cells and their log-end panels. Hanging sign blades carry no text, only the wood's emblem, so DARK OAK is not spelled out anywhere.
The awnings are gone, replaced by the wood-stair lip along the top of each board. The owner didn't ask to lose the awnings, but they covered the names.
I did not touch the interiors, the roof or the grounds, and the sockets are unchanged.
